Absolute Continuity

Shrink the total length of intervals to zero and the total change shrinks too. The Cantor function is a continuous function failing this.

Tiny input changes must not create large outputs. Such functions are exactly the ones built as integrals. The Cantor function stays flat yet climbs from 0 to 1, breaking the rule.

For example, open a tap a little and only a little 💧 water comes out. The Cantor function is a strange tap that pours a bucketful while barely opened.

F absolutely continuous   ⟺  ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0:∑(bi−ai)<δ⇒∑∣F(bi)−F(ai)∣<εF \text{ absolutely continuous } \iff \forall \varepsilon > 0\, \exists \delta > 0: \sum (b_i - a_i) < \delta \Rightarrow \sum |F(b_i) - F(a_i)| < \varepsilonF absolutely continuous ⟺∀ε>0∃δ>0:∑(bi​−ai​)<δ⇒∑∣F(bi​)−F(ai​)∣<ε
F(x)=F(a)+∫axf dx(f∈L1)  ⟺  F absolutely continuousF(x) = F(a) + \int_a^x f\,dx\quad (f \in L^1) \iff F \text{ absolutely continuous}F(x)=F(a)+∫ax​fdx(f∈L1)⟺F absolutely continuous

Prove the Cantor function ccc is not absolutely continuous: the 2n2^n2n stage-nnn Cantor intervals have total length (23)n\left(\frac23\right)^n(32​)n but ∑∣Δc∣=1\sum |\Delta c| = 1∑∣Δc∣=1.

total length=2n⋅3−n=(23)n→0,∑∣Δc∣=2n⋅2−n=1≮12\text{total length} = 2^n \cdot 3^{-n} = \left(\tfrac23\right)^n \to 0, \qquad \sum |\Delta c| = 2^n \cdot 2^{-n} = 1 \not< \tfrac12total length=2n⋅3−n=(32​)n→0,∑∣Δc∣=2n⋅2−n=1<21​
Show proof

  1. Negate absolute continuity: we show that for ε=12\varepsilon = \frac12ε=21​, no δ>0\delta > 0δ>0 can satisfy the condition. The stage-nnn Cantor set consists of 2n2^n2n closed intervals of length 3−n3^{-n}3−n (each interval is trisected and its middle removed).

  2. Their total length is 2n⋅3−n=(23)n→02^n \cdot 3^{-n} = \left(\frac23\right)^n \to 02n⋅3−n=(32​)n→0, so for large nnn the total length is below δ\deltaδ. But the Cantor function ccc rises by exactly 2−n2^{-n}2−n on each stage-nnn interval (fixing the next binary digit of its base-2 expansion).

  3. Hence ∑∣Δc∣=2n⋅2−n=1≮12=ε\sum |\Delta c| = 2^n \cdot 2^{-n} = 1 \not< \frac12 = \varepsilon∑∣Δc∣=2n⋅2−n=1<21​=ε — the sum stays frozen at 1 no matter how small the total length gets.

    This directly violates the definition of absolute continuity, so ccc is not absolutely continuous.

    Since ccc is uniformly continuous, uniform continuity does not imply absolute continuity.

  4. Numerical check (n=4n = 4n=4): total length (23)4=1681≈0.1975\left(\frac23\right)^4 = \frac{16}{81} \approx 0.1975(32​)4=8116​≈0.1975, ∑∣Δc∣=1\sum |\Delta c| = 1∑∣Δc∣=1 — matching the caption. Even at n=10n = 10n=10 the total length shrinks to ≈0.0173\approx 0.0173≈0.0173 while ∑∣Δc∣\sum |\Delta c|∑∣Δc∣ stays 1.
